'''Kuk Young''' ({{Korean|hangul=국양}}; born 1953) is a South Korean physicist, former physics professor and vice-provost of research of [[Seoul National University]], distinguished professor of [[Ewha Womans University]], and chairman of the Samsung Science and Technology Foundation. He is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], [[Korean Academy of Science and Technology]], [[Institute of Physics]], [[Korean Physical Society]], and [[Korean Vacuum Society]]. He has performed editor roles for the journals ''[[Nanotechnology (journal)|Nanotechnology]]'', ''[[ACS Nano]]'', and ''Solid State Electronics''<ref>{{cite web |url= http://nkiss2010.knu.ac.kr/nkiss/2014_session.html |title= More Moore or More than Moore Nano-Devices? |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= 2014 |website= 2014 Session NANO KISS |publisher= Korean International Summer School on Nanoelectronics |access-date= 13 February 2020 |quote=  |language= Korean |archive-date= 18 February 2020 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200218052708/http://nkiss2010.knu.ac.kr/nkiss/2014_session.html |url-status= dead }}</ref> and was the fourth president of [[Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology]] (DGIST). He is best known for his work in the area of surface science and physics in nanometer scale. His interests include geometric and electronic structures of molecular, one-dimensional and surface structures.  

==Education==
Kuk graduated from [[Kyunggi High School]] in 1971 and then went to [[Seoul National University]], where he majored in physics and graduated with a B.S. and M.S. in 1975 and 1978, respectively. Continuing with a physics major, he graduated from [[Pennsylvania State University]] in 1981 with a Ph.D.

== Career ==
With doctorate in hand, Young became a member of the technical staff at [[Bell Labs|AT&T Bell Laboratories]]; a position he continued for a decade.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://people.search.naver.com/search.naver?where=nexearch&query=%EA%B5%AD%EC%96%91&sm=tab_etc&ie=utf8&key=PeopleService&os=159881 |script-title=ko:국양 대학총장 |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= Naver 인물검색 |publisher= [[Naver]] |access-date= 17 February 2020 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref> Returning to Korea in 1991, he became a professor of physics and astronomy at Seoul National University (SNU) for the next 27 years.<ref name=":it">{{cite web |url= http://it.chosun.com/site/data/html_dir/2019/05/17/2019051701905.html |title= "6번의 감사로 휘청거린 DGIST 바로잡겠다" |last= 류 |first= 은주 |date= 18 May 2019 |website= IT Chosun |publisher= |access-date= 17 February 2020 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref> Between March 2002 and December 2004, he was a special committee member for nanoscience within the National Science and Technology Commission. For two years, he was vice-provost for research in the Office of Research Affairs of SNU,<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.ytn.co.kr/_ln/0103_200704271418235489 |script-title=ko:"스널프 스널피 복제늑대 맞다" |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= 27 April 2007 |website= [[YTN]] |publisher= |access-date= 17 February 2020 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref> at the end of which he also became a fellow of the Korean Academy of Science and Technology. For five years he was the chairman of the Samsung Science and Technology Foundation,<ref name=":it"/><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.fnnews.com/news/201904010919589040 |title= DGIST 4대 총장에 국양 삼성미래기술육성재단 이사장 |last= 김 |first= 만기 |date= 1 April 2019 |website=[[The Financial News]] |publisher= |access-date= 17 February 2020 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref> only ending the position upon becoming president of Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology.

In April 2018, he became a distinguished professor at [[Ewha Womans University]],<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.etnews.com/20190326000374 |title= DGIST 제4대 신임 총장에 국양 이화여대 초빙석좌교수 선임 |last= 정 |first= 재훈 |date= 26 March 2019 |website= ET News |publisher= |access-date= 17 February 2020 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.veritas-a.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=126996
